Hot take: UMI data will become the new post-training.

Right now, the most successful models rely on huge amounts of egocentric video data (for example, Build AI shipping the 1M hours dataset Dyna used for its 1-Million-Hour Scaling Law project).

My prediction for the future:
- pre-training will still rely on egocentric video data
- a new mid-training/post-training step using massive amounts of UMI data will be widely adopted
- a final fine-tuning/post-training step will use robot-specific data (teleop etc.) specialized by use case or manufacturer (e.g. Figure using Figure robot data, Optimus using Optimus teleop data etc.) -> similar to what already exists

Why UMI?
Recent research shows it work, enhance results by a large margin, and most importantly: it is the only thing that can scale while being hardware agnotics.

We already have workers wearing hardware for ego video data acquisition.

I expect soon UMI data farms full with workers using UMI grippers around the clock.

Semiconductors/Compute.text:
Broad targeting looks efficient until the churn hits
The spike in lost followers on 2 September lines up with the Broad targeting | Basic ad. The dashboard showed almost 200 new subscribers, but the channel only grew by 30 – then 86% of the subscribers acquired through broad targeting left within hours.
– Broad targeting | Basic follow CR: 3.7%
– MKT channels | Basic follow CR: 1%
– MKT businesses | Basic follow CR: 1.6%
– CTR: 14.42% vs 4.37%
In simple terms, the acquisition signal looked good on paper while the audience did not stick. That is the real problem this Telegram Ads test is pointing to.
Related read:
Telegram Ads: Growth experiment that revealed a money farming machine
